hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 1]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures $54^\circ$ and $58^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 54^\circ - 58^\circ = 68^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is fifty-four degrees. Angle B is fifty-eight degrees. Angle C is sixty-eight degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $JKL$ has angle measures of $68^\circ$ and $54^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 68^\circ - 54^\circ = 58^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle JKL$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle J K L. Angle J is fifty-four degrees. Angle K is fifty-eight degrees. Angle L is sixty-eight degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $MPN$ has angle measures of $47^\circ$ and $51^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 47^\circ - 51^\circ = 82^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle MPN$ is not similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle M N P. Angle M is forty-seven degrees. Angle N is fifty-one degrees. Angle P is eighty-two degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, only $\triangle JKL$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.
